# What To Ask For

> Backend building blocks for AI-built apps. Describe a need in plain words, get the name of the piece, when you need it, 2 to 3 ways to build it, and a copy-paste prompt with acceptance checks.

Agents: fetch /entries.json for everything in one file (search the needs, aliases and keywords fields), or /api/<id>.json for one entry. Each entry page is plain HTML at /e/<id>/index.html.

Each entry in entries.json has a category field. Categories: background (Background work and scheduling), payments (Payments and billing), auth (Auth and accounts), email (Email and notifications), files (Files and uploads), data (Data and databases), security (Security and abuse), deploys (Deploys, uptime and monitoring).

## Entries

### Background work and scheduling

- [Scheduled job](e/scheduled-jobs/index.html): Code that runs on a clock instead of when someone clicks. A scheduler wakes up, checks what is due and runs it. JSON: api/scheduled-jobs.json
- [Background job queue](e/background-job-queue/index.html): The web request saves a job and answers right away. A separate worker picks up the job, does the slow part and stores the result. The page checks back for it. JSON: api/background-job-queue.json
- [Retries with backoff and a dead-letter queue](e/retries-and-dead-letter-queue/index.html): When a call to another service fails, try again after a wait that grows each time, with a little randomness so clients don't all retry at once. After a set number of attempts, park the job in a dead-letter queue or a failed state where a person can see it and replay it. JSON: api/retries-and-dead-letter-queue.json
- [Time zone handling](e/time-zones/index.html): Store moments in time as UTC, store each user's time zone as an IANA name like America/New_York, and convert only when you show a time or schedule one. An offset like -05:00 is not a time zone, because it changes with daylight saving. JSON: api/time-zones.json

### Payments and billing

- [Webhook signature verification](e/webhook-signature-verification/index.html): A webhook is another service calling your URL when something happens. The sender signs each request with a shared secret. Your server recomputes the signature from the raw body and rejects anything that doesn't match or is too old. JSON: api/webhook-signature-verification.json
- [Idempotent webhook handling](e/idempotent-webhooks/index.html): Providers retry webhooks and sometimes deliver the same event more than once or out of order. Idempotent handling means running the same event twice has the same result as running it once. The usual way: save the event id first and skip it if it's already done. JSON: api/idempotent-webhooks.json
- [Subscription billing](e/subscription-billing/index.html): A recurring charge tied to a plan. The payment provider runs the billing schedule. Your app keeps a copy of each customer's subscription status, updated from webhooks, and grants features from that status. Changing plans mid-period creates a proration: a credit for unused time on the old plan and a charge for the new one. JSON: api/subscription-billing.json
- [Failed payment recovery (dunning)](e/failed-payment-recovery/index.html): Renewal charges fail all the time: expired cards, low balances, bank blocks. Dunning is what happens next: retry the charge on a schedule, email the customer a link to update their card, show a banner in the app, and decide when access ends if it never gets paid. JSON: api/failed-payment-recovery.json
- [Usage-based billing](e/usage-based-billing/index.html): Charging for how much someone used instead of a flat fee. Your app records each billable event in its own database first, then reports totals to the billing system, which adds them to the invoice. Prepaid credits are the other common shape: the user buys a balance and each use draws it down. JSON: api/usage-based-billing.json
- [Free trial (with or without a card)](e/free-trials/index.html): A period of paid features before the first charge. Asking for a card up front means fewer people start, but more of them end up paying. Without a card more people try it, and you must decide what happens at the end: cancel, pause, or ask for a card. JSON: api/free-trials.json

### Auth and accounts

- [Password reset tokens](e/password-reset/index.html): A one-time, short-lived link emailed to the account owner that lets them set a new password. The token is random and stored only as a hash (or signed), and it stops working after use, after it expires, and once the password changes. JSON: api/password-reset.json
- [Magic link sign-in](e/magic-links/index.html): The user types their email and gets a link that signs them in. The link holds a random one-time token that expires in minutes. Email security scanners often open links before the person does, so a safe design shows a confirm button and only signs in on that click. JSON: api/magic-links.json
- [Social login (OAuth and OpenID Connect)](e/social-login/index.html): Users sign in with an account they already have. Your app sends them to the provider, gets back a code, and swaps it on the server for tokens that say who they are. Use a library for this, keep the requested permissions small, and only link to an existing account when the provider says the email is verified. JSON: api/social-login.json
- [Sessions vs JWT](e/sessions-vs-jwt/index.html): Two ways to remember who is logged in. A session is a random id in a cookie that points to data on your server, so you can end it any time. A JWT is a signed token that carries the user's details itself, so the server doesn't look anything up, but it stays valid until it expires unless you add a revocation list. JSON: api/sessions-vs-jwt.json
- [Roles and permissions](e/roles-and-permissions/index.html): Rules for who may do what. Users get a role (owner, admin, member, viewer) and each action checks the role on the server. Hiding a button only changes what people see. The server must refuse the request too. JSON: api/roles-and-permissions.json
- [Multi-tenant data isolation](e/multi-tenant-isolation/index.html): Keeping each customer's data separate when they all share one app and one database. Every row carries a tenant id, every query filters on it, and a database rule such as Postgres row level security can act as a second lock in case code forgets. JSON: api/multi-tenant-isolation.json

### Email and notifications

- [Email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC)](e/email-authentication/index.html): Three DNS records that let inbox providers check that mail really comes from you. SPF lists which servers may send for your domain. DKIM signs each message with a key published in DNS. DMARC says what to do when those checks fail and where to send reports. JSON: api/email-authentication.json
- [Transactional vs bulk email](e/transactional-vs-bulk-email/index.html): Transactional email is one message to one person because of something they did: a sign-in link, a receipt, a reset. Bulk email is the same message to many people: newsletters, announcements. Send them through separate streams or providers so complaints about one don't hurt delivery of the other, and send from a background job, not inside the web request. JSON: api/transactional-vs-bulk-email.json
- [Unsubscribe and suppression list](e/unsubscribe-handling/index.html): A way for people to stop marketing email, honored quickly, plus a list of addresses you never mail again: unsubscribes, hard bounces and spam complaints. Gmail requires bulk senders to support one-click unsubscribe through the List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers (RFC 8058). JSON: api/unsubscribe-handling.json
- [Push notifications](e/push-notifications/index.html): Messages that appear on a device even when your app isn't open. On the web, a service worker receives them through the browser's push service, signed with your VAPID keys. iPhones support web push only for sites added to the home screen (iOS 16.4 and later). Native apps use APNs (Apple) and FCM (Google). JSON: api/push-notifications.json

### Files and uploads

- [Signed download link](e/signed-download-links/index.html): A URL with an expiry time and a signature built in. Anyone with the link can download until it expires, and changing any part of it breaks the signature. The files stay private by default. JSON: api/signed-download-links.json

### Data and databases

- [Backups with a tested restore](e/backups-tested-restore/index.html): A backup only counts once you have restored it. Back up the database and uploaded files on a schedule, copy them off the server, and regularly restore into a throwaway database to prove they work. JSON: api/backups-tested-restore.json

### Security and abuse

- [Rate limiting](e/rate-limiting/index.html): Count requests per key (IP address, user or API key) in a time window and refuse with 429 once the count passes the limit. JSON: api/rate-limiting.json
- [Ownership checks (IDOR)](e/ownership-checks/index.html): Checking on every request that the logged-in user is allowed to touch the exact record they asked for. The usual bug: the code loads a record by id and never checks who owns it. Hard-to-guess ids help but don't replace the check. JSON: api/ownership-checks.json
- [Input validation](e/input-validation/index.html): Checking every piece of incoming data on the server against what you expect: type, length, format and allowed values. Anything else is rejected before your code uses it. Browser checks only help the user. Anyone can skip them. JSON: api/input-validation.json

### Deploys, uptime and monitoring

- [Feature flag](e/feature-flags/index.html): A named on and off switch the code checks at runtime. You deploy with the feature off, turn it on for everyone, some users or just yourself, and turn it off fast if it breaks. JSON: api/feature-flags.json
- [Health checks and safe deploys](e/health-checks/index.html): Small URLs your platform calls to ask two things: is the process alive (liveness), and can it serve traffic right now, with the database, cache and migrations in order (readiness). Deploy tools wait for readiness before sending traffic to a new version and keep the old one if it never gets there. JSON: api/health-checks.json

## Data

- [entries.json](entries.json): all entries with prompts and checks
